brief: Access the HR portal and retrieve the layoff order. The account is known; the password is not. Query G-D's Eye for leads, then send password candidates through your botnet. Recon and login requests share one Exposure budget.

facts.label: Public profile
facts.note: Human Remains Manager. His profile links a pet album and a recycled breach record. 'We are not a family. You can't downsize your family every quarter.'

facts.label: Personnel record
facts.note: Alex uses his full birth year in memorable numbers. Reason for employment: 'Not dead yet.'

facts.label: Pet album
facts.note: 'All my important accounts are named after Barsik. People betray you. A cat at least makes eye contact.' His previous cat was called Fluffy. The album links an IT conversation.

facts.label: Old breach
facts.note: No longer valid. Notice the pattern: capitalized name, four-digit year, exclamation mark. Fluffy has since been promoted to cloud storage.

facts.label: IT conversation
facts.value: 'Now I replace lowercase a with @. Name first, year next, ! at the end. Secure enough?'
facts.note: Cross-referencing the pet album and breach record identifies this message after his last password change. IT replied: 'That's my thirteenth reason to quit.'

facts.label: After-hours club
facts.note: The team slogan is 'Strike first, outsource later.' No evidence that this name appears in his current password.

solution.explanation: His current cat is Barsik. Add his birth year, 1990, and follow the old password's capital letter and !. The IT conversation explains a → @. You cracked a habit, not a cipher.
